title: Evidence first. Judgement stays human.
intro: What LabourLens contributes today, what the results actually show, and what I would add before policy makers could rely on it.
contribution_intro: The contribution is not a new model. It is a way of keeping a research answer connected to its evidence, its calculation and its limits.

contributions.title: Answers with an evidence trail
contributions.text: Validated statistical records and source passages sit behind the answer, with claim citations and observation lineage for inspection.
contributions.detail: Numbers should come from validated tables or deterministic code. Citation checks establish mechanics, not that every claim is semantically supported.

contributions.title: The right quarter, the right release
contributions.text: Period and release filters narrow the evidence before reranking, keeping preliminary and final releases distinguishable.
contributions.detail: A later report can restate an earlier quarter. A hard period filter can still exclude useful evidence; conflict caveats do not guarantee that every revision is resolved.

contributions.title: Arithmetic outside the model
contributions.text: Typed, read-only tools retrieve series and calculate changes in code rather than asking the model to do the sums.
contributions.detail: Deterministic arithmetic can still use the wrong series or periods. Report-table arithmetic remains a weakness; the attempted tool extension failed its criteria and was not adopted.

contributions.title: An agent with boundaries
contributions.text: A bounded research graph uses typed state, read-only tools, stopping conditions and visible task traces, with abstention when evidence is missing.
contributions.detail: A working MCP server exposes evidence capabilities. The live route sends the statistics tool over MCP; all three tools over MCP is a measured option, not the live route.

contributions.title: Experiments that keep the losses
contributions.text: Pre-registered comparisons, frozen outputs, gold hashes and three question sets make the design decisions inspectable.
contributions.detail: Development questions shaped the system. The original test shares evidence with development; the fresh questions use different sources, but their outcomes are now known. Negative results stay in the record.

contributions.title: Defence in layers
contributions.text: Untrusted-text isolation, an ingestion scanner, constrained tools and attack tests reduce the authority given to retrieved text.
contributions.detail: The scanner is a warning layer, not a safety boundary. The attack suite is hand-written and shows no general defence effect; a planted false figure is not handled consistently across runs.

roadmap_title: From research tool to government workbench
roadmap_intro: Six questions from the assessment shape this plan. Every addition below is a proposal, not a shipped feature. I assume public data only, an analyst in the decision loop and a government-approved deployment; none is evidence of production readiness.

roadmap.name: Improve retrieval and answer quality
roadmap.purpose: Fix missing numerical evidence before adding more model complexity.

items.title: Start with the observed failures
items.why: Current retrieval hit@8 rises from 0.539 to 0.969 on 128 development questions, but neither final test set demonstrates an answer-quality gain. Historical fresh-set numerical comparisons scored 0.214 (3 of 14); the attempted tool extension failed its criteria and was not adopted.

items.title: Extract tables with verified definitions
items.why: Validate PDF table cells, units, populations and row/column lineage before making them calculable. Treat table_unreliable passages as insufficient evidence rather than letting a model infer the cells; test period restatements so a later report is not excluded by a hard period filter.

items.title: Expand only after a quality gate
items.why: Add missing quarters, MOM, MTI and SingStat series and languages only with reviewed provenance, revision history and language-specific evaluation. Wider coverage is useful only if definitions and uncertainty remain visible.

roadmap.name: Detect and respond to change
roadmap.purpose: Hold a release when changing evidence or behaviour causes an unexplained regression.

items.title: Version inputs and rerun the gate
items.why: Extend corpus fingerprints and gold-hash checks into release control: check schemas, missing quarters and revisions, then rerun evaluation on every corpus, prompt or model change. Retain the previous version and roll back on an unexplained regression.

items.title: Watch retrieval, answers and providers
items.why: Track retrieval hit rate on reviewed probes, abstention, citation validity, grounded-number rate, latency and cost per question. Use a fixed embedding probe set, pin model versions where available and alert on provider changes; daily canaries would detect drift between releases.

items.title: Watch researchers' changing needs
items.why: Sample minimised, pseudonymised audit logs and feedback for changing question families, clarification rates and unsupported requests. Analysts would review the shift before changing coverage; pseudonymisation does not remove all privacy risk.

roadmap.name: Support confidence and human review
roadmap.purpose: Show evidence and disagreement, not an invented confidence probability.

items.title: Make each answer inspectable
items.why: Build on passage citations, observation lineage, abstention reasons, conflict flags, the evidence drawer and tool-call traces. Add table-row locators, side-by-side sources and evidence-coverage indicators, not hidden reasoning or a model self-rating.

items.title: Turn feedback into reviewed cases
items.why: Existing feedback capture would feed an analyst queue: classify the failure, draft a regression case, adjudicate it and rerun one controlled change. Saved analyses, exportable cited briefings and revision alerts would preserve that trail for policy work.

items.title: Check quality independently
items.why: Several reviewers would label before seeing AI suggestions, measure agreement and adjudicate disagreements. Add a second-family judge at full scale and repeated runs; today's AI-drafted gold, one reviewer and same-family main judge cannot establish independent accuracy.

roadmap.name: Manage privacy and third-party risk
roadmap.purpose: Replace demo admission with accountable access and an approved processing boundary.

items.title: Clear rights and protect identities
items.why: Review data licences, report rights and publisher agreements, then replace shared demo access codes with government SSO and role-based source permissions. Set approved audit retention, restricted log access and pseudonymised records; use only public or approved synthetic data in this prototype.

items.title: Approve hosting and model use
items.why: Data residency and private model endpoints require government approval; the current external model route is not an approved replacement. Provider data-use terms remain unverified. Review processing terms and keep a vendor exit plan with exportable evidence, a tested alternative endpoint and evaluation before switching.

items.title: Keep untrusted content untrusted
items.why: Retain read-only tools, bounded calls and the MCP trust boundary; add an independently tested injection classifier, server allow-lists, incident ownership and recurring red-team checks. Scanner detections rose from 10 to 23 of 30, with 9 of 30 benign flags unchanged; it remains a warning layer.

items.title: Fail safely, without fake services
items.why: On provider failure, return an explicit unavailable result or previously approved cached analysis, never an unvalidated model fallback. No live service on this page is mocked; hostile-server fixtures are synthetic tests, not government identity or hosting. Production replacements need approved SSO, private infrastructure and a reviewed provider contract.

roadmap.name: Control latency and cost
roadmap.purpose: Keep the expensive steps only when their measured quality benefit justifies them.

items.title: Use the measured budget, not a promise
items.why: Primary development filter-then-rerank means are 14.35 s for run medians and $0.002845 per question; run p95 values are 35.4 s and 34.1 s. Costs are list-price estimates. All-three-tools MCP scored 0.877 versus 0.908 for the live statistics-only route, with median 14.3 versus 12.4 s and p95 51.4 versus 34.7 s: slower, no demonstrated gain, not live.

items.title: Cache and route under quality tests
items.why: Retain embedding caches and test version-keyed retrieval or answer caches, filter-only routing and smaller models for triage or reranking. Cache invalidation must follow source revisions; cheaper routing must preserve citation support, numerical correctness and abstention behaviour.

items.title: Set budgets and stop on overruns
items.why: Add per-question token, call, latency and cost budgets, p95 alerts and provider spending limits with named response owners. Proposed acceptance is p95 under 40 s and mean cost under $0.005 per question on the approved evaluation mix, with no quality regression; application reservations alone are not provider caps.

roadmap.name: Prioritise two measurable improvements
roadmap.purpose: First make report figures usable; then establish an independent estimate of quality.

items.title: First: validated report-table arithmetic
items.why: Pre-register a single extraction-and-tool change. Use the known 14 fresh-set numerical questions as a regression set, not new-test evidence: target at least 0.50 accuracy versus the historical 0.214, no rise in all-question false-answer rate on a fixed paired suite, and unchanged definition/citation checks. Confirm on newly written blind numerical questions; reject the change if the safety or quality gate fails.

items.title: Second: independent review and a blind set
items.why: Have at least three analysts independently label a stratified, newly written blind set before seeing AI outputs, then adjudicate. Target Fleiss' kappa at least 0.70 on behaviour labels and a 95% case-bootstrap headline accuracy interval no wider than 0.10; pre-register sampling and expand the sample if needed. Report disagreement, claim support, numerical correctness and run variance separately, without tuning on this set.

limits: I would not call this production ready for government or a substitute for an analyst's judgement.
Gold was AI-drafted and reviewed by one person after AI pre-review and scoring, not independently labelled by several analysts.
The main judge is from the same model family. The three question sets are only partially independent, and neither final test set demonstrates a retrieval-driven answer-quality gain.
A citation is not proof of truth, a correct calculation is not proof of the right inputs, and a scanner pass is not proof of safety.
Rights clearance, provider data-use terms and the population basis of the employment series remain unverified.
